text:
Juno Park: Quick review request  bulk edit confirmation dialog copy. Current: 'Apply changes to 120 items. This cannot be undone.' Feels blunt. Screenshot: https://redwood/mockups/bulk-edit-confirm.png

Marco Ruiz: Agree  users need a clearer summary of what's changing and an easy escape. Maybe add a line that lists the change types and a reversible path (if any).

Leah Kim: Draft variant: "Apply changes to 120 items?
This will update name, visibility, and quota settings. Changes are immediate. Some changes can be reverted from each item's settings." Buttons: [Cancel] [Apply changes]

Omar Hassan: I like listing the fields. Two accessibility/UX points: 
- Make Cancel the default focus.
- Add a small expandable summary (collapsed by default) that shows examples, so the dialog stays short but details are available.

Juno Park: Good call. For the short line maybe: "Apply updates to 120 items: name, visibility, quota. Changes apply immediately." Then a "See details" disclosure with the full list.

Marco Ruiz: Tone nit: avoid 'immediately' alone  users interpret that as 'no undo'. Add 'can be reverted where supported' or link to docs. e.g., "Changes apply immediately; some can be reverted per item."

Leah Kim: Accessibility checklist from me:
- Dialog should have `aria-labelledby` for the question line and `aria-describedby` for the short summary.
- Disclosure summary must be keyboard operable and announce expanded state.
- Buttons need explicit aria-labels if we include item counts: `Apply changes to 120 items`.

Omar Hassan: Also add microcopy near the Apply button: small helper text "Affected items: 120" so keyboard users see scope when focusing the action.

A11yBot: Created task: a11y/dialogs - bulk-edit confirmation (disclosure semantics, focus, live region for applying progress). See /docs/a11y/disclosures.

Juno Park: I'll update Figma with the concise line + expandable details and push a small PR with the copy + aria attributes. Will include the helper text by the action.

Marco Ruiz: Thanks  @Leah please review the PR when it's up?

Leah Kim: Will do. :thumbsup:
